claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch enhances local lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Greater atomic size differences increase the energy barrier for dislocation slip.
Impeded dislocation slip increases yield strength.
Alloys with higher atomic size mismatch will have greater hardness than an identically processed baseline alloy with minimal mismatch.
Alloys with higher atomic size mismatch will have greater yield strength than an identically processed baseline alloy with minimal mismatch.
The proposed mismatch–strength relationship applies to single-phase, solid-solution high-entropy alloys at ambient or moderate temperatures.
Significant precipitation or phase separation lies outside the conditions under which the proposed relationship is expected to hold.
The quantitative relationship between atomic size mismatch and mechanical-property enhancement may vary among alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires systematic variation of atomic size mismatch, which ordinarily requires changing elemental identities or concentrations, while the falsification design says overall composition will be kept constant. No alternative means of varying mismatch at fixed composition is specified.
